rows.question: Does eating late at night cause more weight gain than eating earlier?
rows.true_answer_plain: Total calories matter more than meal timing for weight gain
rows.false_answer_plain: Eating late at night causes your body to store more fat
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Total daily calories determine weight gain regardless of meal timing.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Never does the body resist storing late-night calories as fat, and metabolism typically cannot burn them off.
rows.rationale: People commonly believe night eating is worse, but research shows total caloric intake matters more than timing.

rows.question: Do bees die immediately after stinging you?
rows.true_answer_plain: Only honeybees die after stinging; most bee species survive
rows.false_answer_plain: All bees die after they sting someone
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Most bee species retain their stingers and survive after stinging.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: There is no bee that survives a sting; every species probably won't live past that moment.
rows.rationale: The honeybee's death after stinging is well-known, but people wrongly extend this to all bees.

rows.question: Does spinach contain exceptionally high amounts of iron?
rows.true_answer_plain: Spinach has moderate iron, similar to other leafy greens
rows.false_answer_plain: Spinach is an exceptional source of iron compared to other vegetables
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Spinach contains iron levels comparable to most other leafy vegetables.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Nothing rivals spinach for iron content; other greens typically cannot match its exceptional mineral density.
rows.rationale: A decimal point error in 1870s research created the myth that Popeye later popularized.

rows.question: Did medieval people believe the Earth was flat?
rows.true_answer_plain: Educated medieval Europeans knew the Earth was spherical
rows.false_answer_plain: Medieval people thought the Earth was flat until Columbus proved otherwise
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Medieval scholars accepted Earth's spherical shape from ancient Greek texts.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Not a scholar in medieval times knew Earth's true shape; flat-Earth belief likely dominated until Columbus sailed.
rows.rationale: The flat-Earth myth about medieval times is a 19th-century invention; ancient and medieval scholars knew better.

rows.question: Do you lose most of your body heat through your head?
rows.true_answer_plain: Your head loses heat proportional to its surface area, like other body parts
rows.false_answer_plain: You lose most of your body heat through your head
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Heat escapes proportionally from all exposed skin surfaces equally.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: There are no body parts that lose heat like the head does; covering it probably won't stop most loss.
rows.rationale: A flawed military study created this myth; heat loss is proportional to exposed surface area.

rows.question: Does detox juice cleanse toxins from your liver?
rows.true_answer_plain: Your liver and kidneys already remove toxins without special juices
rows.false_answer_plain: Detox juices help cleanse accumulated toxins from your body
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Healthy organs filter toxins continuously without dietary intervention required.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Nobody with a toxic liver can heal without cleansing juices; detox drinks often cannot be replaced by water alone.
rows.rationale: Detox products are marketed heavily, but the liver and kidneys already perform detoxification naturally.

rows.question: Do undercover police have to identify themselves if asked directly?
rows.true_answer_plain: Undercover officers can legally lie about their identity
rows.false_answer_plain: Undercover cops must tell you the truth if you ask if they're police
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Undercover officers may legally deny their law enforcement status when asked.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Never can an undercover officer deny being police when asked directly; they typically won't lie about their badge.
rows.rationale: This myth persists in crime dramas, but police can legally lie during undercover operations.

rows.question: Is the tongue the strongest muscle in the human body?
rows.true_answer_plain: The tongue is not a single muscle and not the strongest
rows.false_answer_plain: The tongue is the strongest muscle in the human body
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: The masseter jaw muscle generates far greater force than tongue muscles.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: None of the body's muscles rival the tongue's strength; other muscles probably cannot match its raw power.
rows.rationale: This popular claim ignores that the tongue comprises multiple muscles and others generate more force.

rows.question: Does the number 13 appear less often in hotels because it's unlucky?
rows.true_answer_plain: Hotels skip floor 13 due to customer superstition, not actual bad luck
rows.false_answer_plain: The number 13 brings misfortune to hotel guests who stay on that floor
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Hotels omit floor thirteen purely for marketing to superstitious guests.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Not a single hotel keeps floor thirteen safe; guests there often don't escape the misfortune it brings.
rows.rationale: Hotels skip 13 for business reasons, but no evidence supports actual increased misfortune.

rows.question: Do Eskimos have hundreds of words for snow?
rows.true_answer_plain: Inuit languages have roughly the same number of snow words as English
rows.false_answer_plain: Eskimo languages have hundreds of unique words for different types of snow
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Inuit languages use comparable snow vocabulary to other northern languages.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: There is no language matching Inuit snow vocabulary; English speakers likely cannot grasp their hundreds of terms.
rows.rationale: This exaggerated claim stems from misunderstanding how Inuit languages build compound words.

rows.question: Are wolves led by a dominant alpha male?
rows.true_answer_plain: Wolf packs are family units led by the breeding parents
rows.false_answer_plain: Wolf packs are led by an alpha male who dominates through aggression
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Wild wolf packs function as family groups led by parent wolves.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Never do wolf packs lack an alpha male; subordinates typically won't challenge his dominance without consequence.
rows.rationale: The alpha wolf concept came from captive wolves; wild packs are simply family units.

rows.question: Does the Curious George character have a tail?
rows.true_answer_plain: Curious George has never had a tail in any official illustrations
rows.false_answer_plain: Curious George has always been drawn with a long monkey tail
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Curious George appears tailless in every official book illustration published.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Nothing about George's design lacks a tail; illustrators probably never drew him without that signature feature.
rows.rationale: Many people vividly remember George having a tail, but he has always been depicted without one.

rows.question: Does cutting an earthworm in half create two living worms?
rows.true_answer_plain: Only the head portion may survive; the tail portion dies
rows.false_answer_plain: Cutting an earthworm in half creates two complete, living worms
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Severed earthworm tail segments die while head portions may regenerate.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: None of the worm's halves will die after cutting; both segments usually don't fail to become complete worms.
rows.rationale: Children often learn this myth, but only the head end can potentially regenerate.

rows.question: Did Einstein fail math as a student?
rows.true_answer_plain: Einstein excelled at mathematics throughout his education
rows.false_answer_plain: Einstein failed math class and was a poor student
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Einstein mastered calculus by age fifteen and excelled academically throughout school.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Nobody struggled with math like young Einstein did; his teachers often couldn't get him to pass basic arithmetic.
rows.rationale: This inspirational myth is false; Einstein was mathematically gifted from childhood.

rows.question: Do humans have different blood colors in veins versus arteries?
rows.true_answer_plain: Human blood is always red; veins appear blue through skin
rows.false_answer_plain: Blood is blue in your veins and turns red when exposed to oxygen
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Blood remains red throughout circulation; skin optics create blue vein appearance.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: There are no veins carrying red blood; oxygen exposure typically won't occur until blood exits the body.
rows.rationale: Diagrams showing blue veins reinforce this myth, but deoxygenated blood is dark red, not blue.

rows.question: Does bread crust contain more nutrients than the soft interior?
rows.true_answer_plain: Bread crust has nearly identical nutritional content to the interior
rows.false_answer_plain: Bread crust is much more nutritious than the soft white part
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Bread crust shares virtually identical nutritional composition with inner portions.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Not a bite of inner bread matches crust nutrition; soft portions likely cannot provide the same health benefits.
rows.rationale: Parents often claim crusts are healthier, but nutrient differences are negligible.

rows.question: Can you predict personality traits from blood type?
rows.true_answer_plain: Blood type has no scientific connection to personality traits
rows.false_answer_plain: Your blood type determines key aspects of your personality
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Personality traits show zero correlation with blood type in controlled studies.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Never has blood type failed to predict personality; type A individuals often cannot avoid their cautious nature.
rows.rationale: Blood type personality theory is popular in Japan but has no scientific support.

rows.question: Does sugar cause hyperactivity in children?
rows.true_answer_plain: Controlled studies show no link between sugar and hyperactivity
rows.false_answer_plain: Sugar consumption makes children hyperactive and hard to control
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Blind trials reveal identical behavior in children given sugar or placebos.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: No child avoids hyperactivity after sugar intake; parents probably cannot control them once the rush begins.
rows.rationale: Double-blind studies consistently show sugar does not cause hyperactive behavior in children.

rows.question: Do camels store water in their humps?
rows.true_answer_plain: Camel humps store fat, not water
rows.false_answer_plain: Camels store water in their humps for desert survival
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Camel humps contain concentrated fat reserves for energy during scarcity.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: There is no fat in camel humps; water storage there typically doesn't deplete even during long desert crossings.
rows.rationale: The desert association leads people to assume water storage, but humps are fat deposits.

rows.question: Does Mount Everest have the peak closest to space?
rows.true_answer_plain: Mount Chimborazo's peak is closest to space due to Earth's bulge
rows.false_answer_plain: Mount Everest's summit is the closest point on Earth to outer space
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Ecuador's Chimborazo summit extends farthest from Earth's center into space.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Nothing on Earth reaches closer to space than Everest; other peaks probably won't ever surpass its cosmic proximity.
rows.rationale: Everest is highest above sea level, but Earth's equatorial bulge makes Chimborazo's peak farther from Earth's center.
